statement.plain_text: If p is prime and a is not divisible by p, then a^(p-1) ≡ 1 mod p.
statement.markdown: If $p$ is prime and $p \nmid a$, then $a^{p-1} \equiv 1 \pmod p$.
statement.latex: p\text{ prime},\ p\nmid a \implies a^{p-1}\equiv 1 \pmod p

proof_outline_steps.plain_text: Multiply each nonzero residue class modulo p by a.
proof_outline_steps.markdown: Multiply each nonzero residue class modulo $p$ by $a$.

proof_outline_steps.plain_text: Because a is invertible modulo p, this multiplication permutes the nonzero residues.
proof_outline_steps.markdown: Because $a$ is invertible modulo $p$, this multiplication permutes the nonzero residues.

proof_outline_steps.plain_text: Compare the product of the permuted list to the original list and cancel the common factors.
proof_outline_steps.markdown: Compare the product of the permuted list to the original list and cancel the common factors.
